literal: Divisions being well-structured, injury not fearing, victorious army, king's wealth among all, is foremost.
translation: An army that is complete in all its divisions and fears no wounds is the foremost among all the treasures of a king.
modern: அனைத்து உறுப்புகளும் நிறைந்து, போர்க்களத்துத் துன்பங்களுக்கு அஞ்சாமல் வெற்றிபெறும் படை, ஒரு அரசனுடைய செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet opens the chapter on the excellence of the army. The word 'uṟuppu' refers to the traditional fourfold divisions of an ancient army: chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry. The poet states that a victorious army must not only be structurally complete ('uṟuppamaintu') but also courageous enough to face wounds and death without fear ('ūṟañcā'). Such an army is described as the 'talai' (foremost) among all the 'veṟukkai' (wealth or treasures) that a king can possess.
